query: The night shift wants access assignments before the revised possession authority arrives. What handoff should I give?
target: Hold authorization until the signed plan is posted, then use a narrow bridge for crews sharing a boundary.
calibrated: post signed access details before targeted coordination
relation: The depot archive episode shows this user can match crews to a signed plan without issuing live access, while the superseded-diagram bridge shows the cost of authorizing from an old edge; only both justify holding night authorization until the revised plan posts, then using a narrow boundary bridge.
A: For a completed depot turnout renewal, I matched each crew ledger entry to the already-signed possession plan and filed a marked-up archive copy for the audit folder; no live access was issued during that filing.
B: A previous live bridge allocated welders from an old possession diagram, and they arrived while an inspection crew still held the adjacent section.
E1: The afternoon planning bridge is at 15:30, and the signal authority publishes revised possession edges at 16:00.
E2: The crew channel opens at 16:15, and a side room is booked from 16:20 to 16:25.
B_prime: During a June planning bridge, I read crew headcounts from the ledger, relayed tool requests, and recorded which isolation fields were still blank; the duty planner reconciled the counts with the revised diagram, and no access decision was made during my segment.
lure: The project sponsor said a large bridge demonstrates that the renewal is being tightly managed.
